name: Position control
description: An integral position controller with rate feedback: voltage accumulates for as long as the link's angle differs from the live setpoint (the integral term), while a rate term opposes the link's own angular velocity (damping, the same role a derivative term plays in a standard PID). Pure integral action alone is not enough here -- driving a plant with two more integrators (current and angular velocity feeding into angle) through a third pure integrator (voltage) is a fourth-order loop with no inherent damping, and is unstable for any positive gain, not just a large one. The rate term is what actually closes the loop safely. Connect from a Rotational link to a Voltage source, then scrub the setpoint live during a run.
